uncertain.note: the mark after the italic marker a is a small roundish blob sitting on/just below the baseline; read as a period, but a comma cannot be excluded at 9x

uncertain.note: 'meuztre' sic for meurtre: the fourth letter matches the z of 'accuſez' (flat top bar, diagonal, foot bar) and not the r of 'par'; wrong sort in the forme
a small mark stands above the e of 'Ode'; read as the swash tip of the italic d (the same shape appears over 'de' in note a), not an accent
numeral read as iij (three stems, three dots); Horace Carm. III.11 is the Hypermnestra ode, which fits
the letter between 'fallaci' and 'er' is the odd italic t (curled top, §2) and reads very like an r; the word must be fallaciter. Ink here is the faintest on the page
the second word's first letter has a crossbar on both sides of the stem (italic f, as in 'fallaciter'), not the left-nub long ſ of 'accuſa'; read 'fi.' (capitulo finali), not 'ſi.'
signature reads C ij (open C, no bars); on folio 35 an E or F would be expected by gathering count, but the letter printed is a C

a raised wave-shaped stroke stands over the u of 'au' and is read as a printed tilde (ũ), a wrong sort since sense wants plain 'au'; it could be an ink accident on a heavily inked sort. Kept as printed.
specks over the n of 'fin' and over 'de' read as ink spatter, not tildes; the print sets '.C.' with the point before the C, normalized per §1.
numerals small and lightly inked; read iij (three stems, as wide as the 'iij' of 'q. iij.' below) and viij.

decisions.reason: At 5x the fourth sort is a z: flat top bar, diagonal, flat foot bar, no bowl or shoulder; the r of 'tre' and 'par' on the same line is a plain stem with a hooked arm. Wrong sort, transcribed as printed (sic).

At 8x a raised wave-shaped stroke sits centred over the u, the same weight and height as the tilde of 'calũnia' two notes down; not a random blot (a separate speck lies to its right). Printed ũ (wrong sort for 'au'), kept as printed with an uncertain entry.

At 7x the mark over the n is a short dot/tick like the i-dot beside it, not a horizontal bar; 'de' on the same line carries similar specks. No tilde. The point before C is printed '.C.' and normalized per §1.
At 7x the first numeral has three stems (i, i, j with descender) and is as wide as the 'iij' of 'q. iij.' two lines below, twice the 'ij' of 'Paulum. ij.'; viij confirmed (v + three stems).
At 4x the letter has a crossbar on both sides of the stem (italic f, as in 'fallaciter' above), unlike the left-nub ſ of 'accuſa' in note a. 'illec' has a closed-bowl e before the c.

The alphabet restarts at ANNOT. XIX. on this page (first-run b from p034's a, then a b c d). Per §4 and the p031 precedent a same-page restart is keyed a, b2, c2, d2 in body and margin; both readers only renumbered the colliding b. Body markers changed to {c2} and {d2} to match.
